title: How a trebuchet uses a falling weight to throw
examples: How does a trebuchet throw so far?
Why does a trebuchet have a heavy weight?
Why is the trebuchet arm so long on one side?

explain.say: A trebuchet is a giant lever. A long beam pivots on a tall frame, with a heavy counterweight on the short end and a sling holding a stone on the long end.

draw.text: How a trebuchet uses a falling weight to throw

explain.say: The counterweight is so heavy that its turning effect, its weight times its distance from the pivot, is far bigger than the stone's. So when released, the counterweight side drops.
The stone's end is much further from the pivot, so as the short end falls a little, the long end swings through a huge arc very fast. The sling adds even more length and speed.
Energy stored by lifting the counterweight becomes the stone's motion energy. Medieval trebuchets could hurl stones of 100 kilograms or more hundreds of metres.

faq.q: Why does a trebuchet have a heavy weight?
faq.a: The counterweight stores energy when it is raised. As it falls, its large turning effect swings the arm, turning that stored energy into the stone's motion.

faq.q: Why is the trebuchet arm so long on one side?
faq.a: The stone's end of the beam is far from the pivot, so it moves much further and faster than the counterweight end in the same time. A long arm trades force for speed.
asks: Why is the stone far from the pivot?

faq.a: The sling acts like an extra length of arm that whips round. It adds speed and releases the stone at the right moment when one loop slips off a hook.
asks: Why does a trebuchet use a sling?

faq.q: How does a trebuchet throw so far?
faq.a: A big falling weight provides lots of energy, the long arm and sling turn it into high speed, and fast stones fly far.
asks: How far can a trebuchet throw?

faq.a: Counterweight trebuchets were used in the Middle East and Europe from about the 12th century until gunpowder cannons replaced them.

facts: Counterweight trebuchets appeared around the 12th century.
The Warwolf, a giant trebuchet built for Edward I, was used at the siege of Stirling Castle in 1304.

quiz.say: Why does the stone end of a trebuchet move so fast?
quiz.show: Why does the stone end of a trebuchet move so fast?

options.show: It is much further from the pivot
options.say: It is much further from the pivot

quiz.why: Points further from the pivot travel a bigger arc in the same time, so they move faster.

wrong.1: The stone is much lighter than the counterweight.
wrong.2: Trebuchets use a falling weight, not gunpowder.
